code-to-image.name: Code to Image
code-to-image.tagline: Turn code snippets into beautiful shareable images with syntax highlighting and themes.
code-to-image.metaTitle: Code to Image - Beautiful Code Screenshots Free | JaurTools
code-to-image.metaDescription: Convert code to beautiful images online for free. Syntax highlighting, dark/light themes, line numbers. Download PNG for posts and docs. No sign-up.
code-to-image.keywords: code to image, code screenshot generator, beautiful code snippet image, syntax highlight image
code-to-image.quickAnswer: Paste your code, pick dark or light theme, and the tool renders it as a styled image: macOS-style header dots, language label, line numbers, and syntax highlighting for keywords, strings, comments, and numbers. A 12-line snippet at 16 px font renders roughly 760 x 430 px. Download the PNG for Twitter, blogs, and docs.
keyFacts: Syntax highlighting covers keywords, strings, comments, numbers, and function calls.
Two themes: dark editor (like VS Code) and clean light paper.
Line numbers are optional and sit in a subtle gutter.
The canvas sizes itself to your code — no wasted empty space.
Monospace font keeps columns aligned exactly like your editor.
Output PNG is crisp at 2x-style rendering for retina screens.
howTo: Paste or type your code in the text box.
Type the language name for the header label (e.g. TypeScript).
Choose the dark or light theme and set the font size.
Toggle line numbers on or off.
Check the preview, then click Download to save the PNG.
code-to-image.formula:
lineHeight = fontSize x 1.5
canvasWidth = maxLineWidth + gutter + 2 x padding
canvasHeight = headerHeight + lines x lineHeight + 2 x padding
Example: 12 lines at 16 px -> lineHeight 24; height = 64 + 288 + 64 = 416 px plus padding.
code-to-image.workedExample:
12 lines, longest line 60 chars, font 16 px, dark theme:
1. lineHeight = 16 x 1.5 = 24 px.
2. Text width: 60 chars x ~9.6 px = ~576 px; gutter 48 + padding 2x32 = 112 -> canvas ~688 px wide.
3. Height: header 56 + 12 x 24 = 288 + padding 64 = ~408 px.
4. Result: a ~688 x 408 PNG that looks like a polished editor screenshot.
benefits: Share code on social media without ugly plain-text screenshots.
Consistent branding: same theme across all your snippets.
No editor setup or extensions needed — paste and download.
Light theme prints beautifully in documents and PDFs.
Your code never leaves the browser — private snippets stay private.
limitations: Highlighting is regex-based, not a full parser — exotic syntax may mis-color.
One snippet per image; multi-file diffs are not supported.
Font is fixed monospace; custom font upload is not available.
Very long lines scroll visually — keep lines under ~80 chars for best results.
code-to-image.privacyNote: This tool runs 100% in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.

faqs.a: The highlighter recognizes common keywords, strings, comments, and numbers across C-like languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C#, Python, and more). The language label in the header is free text, so any language name works there.
The two built-in themes (dark and light) have fixed palettes tuned for readability. Custom palettes are not available in this version — pick the theme that matches where you will post the image.

faqs.q: Why does my long line get cut off?
faqs.a: The canvas grows to fit your longest line, so nothing is cut — but very long lines make the image very wide. Wrap lines around 80 characters for images that read well on phones.

faqs.q: Is this better than a screenshot?
faqs.a: Usually yes: no window chrome, no inconsistent fonts, no background clutter, and consistent padding and colors every time. Plus the PNG is generated at high resolution so text stays sharp.

faqs.q: Can I hide the line numbers?
faqs.a: Yes — toggle them off for a cleaner look, especially for short snippets shared on social media.

faqs.q: Is my code uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. Rendering happens entirely in your browser. Proprietary code never leaves your device.
